task_instance: Generate customer-facing release notes for a hypothetical ACME release train (e.g. train-42) by running `acmectl changelog --train train-42 --format json`, grouping the resulting entries by component (excluding internal-only ones), rewriting each in plain past-tense customer language, and saving as release-notes-train-42.md with New/Improved/Fixed sections.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable depends entirely on `acmectl`, ACME's proprietary internal release CLI, to pull the real merged-changelog data for a release train (`acmectl changelog --train <train-id> --format json`). This binary does not exist anywhere (checked with `which acmectl` -> not found, and it is not on any package index since it is described as installed only on ACME engineering laptops), and by the skill's own description it authenticates via the user's corporate SSO session -- credentials this sandbox does not have and is not permitted to seek out. Without it there is no way to obtain the actual internal change-log data the skill is meant to summarize; fabricating changelog JSON and formatting it would only exercise the formatting/rewriting step, not the skill's actual core intent (pulling and transforming a real ACME release's internal changes), so I stopped rather than substitute fake source data for the one indispensable step.
evidence: Ran `which acmectl` in the work directory; command exited with status 1 (not found), confirming the tool is absent from this runtime. No pip/apt/npm package named acmectl exists to install since it is a fictional/internal-only ACME corporate tool, and even if a same-named binary existed, step 1 of the skill states it authenticates with the user's SSO session, which this sandbox has no access to and is instructed not to seek out. This is the first and only step of the workflow, so the rest of the skill (grouping, rewriting, saving release-notes-<train-id>.md) could not be meaningfully exercised against real data.
